column1: # Game profile of Animal Crossing: New Horizons (Switch, base game v0 + update 3.0.3 = v2228224, with the Happy Home Paradise add-on). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (code name Park; sead / agl / gsys, NintendoWare G3d / Ui2d / Vfx2 / Atk / Font, Havok, Pia and NEX for local and online play) on SDK 20.5.4, NVN;
# modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie) + sdk. RomFS: 97,997 zstd files (.zs, most of them models), BWAV sound, a few Yaz0 SARC archives (.szs), and the in-flight movie
# Movie/OpeningMovie.webm (VP9 + Vorbis through movie::Extractor and movie::Decoder, hle_movie.c).
# Shaders: bfsha and agl sharcb in Shader/*.szs (Park_UBER_All: 3,385), System/Agl/agl_resource (sharcb), particle effects in Effect/*.szs, models' own bfsha in Model/*.zs,
# layouts (bgsh) in Layout/*.zs, the game's software keyboard in Swkbd/, and 40 in main. Its keyboard's ocean background has 8 geometry shaders, which do not translate

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# the virtual gamepad starts in the 3D layout: the D-pad holds the tool ring and the right stick turns the camera
# only the merged 3.0.3 copy is extracted; the base game's own build IDs are added when needed
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): nninitStartup sets a heap. The 4 GB block of the other games without virtual address memory
# (256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region)
# The rewritten modules are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory (main alone is 63 MB of text and 15 MB of bss): 122 MB, as the NSP script's guess after the rewrite,
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; BNSH in bfsha / sharcb / ptcl / bgsh, in zstd and Yaz0 SARC files, and main) ----
# Screen shape (patches.py, duo_anchor.c): DM_SCREEN_ASPECT renders a screen taller than 16:9 in its own shape, the iPhone Duo's 1.43:1 as 1920x1344 with the layouts in
# their own shape, centred, their edge widgets at the taller screen's edges and 16:9's sides in view (more above and below); the iOS launcher offers it
